- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.4), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 periods ahead.
- Model underperforms in early horizon (1–5 days) when sentiment is volatile; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: average last 3 sentiment values to adjust forecast slope.
- If sentiment is flat (0.2–0.4) and price is trending upward, model often fails to capture momentum; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive abruptly, model lags; forecast should adjust 1–2 days ahead of sentiment change.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate in high-sentiment periods; apply a 2–4% downward bias if sentiment >0.7 over last 7 days.
- If sentiment is low and price is near historical mean, model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid mean-reversion trap.
